'''''Gladiolus illyricus''''', the '''wild gladiolus''', is a [[flowering plant]] in the family ''[[Iridaceae]]''.<ref name=POWO>{{cite web |url= https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:20008765-1 |title= Gladiolus illyricus W.D.J.Koch |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=The Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=April 17, 2025}}</ref><ref name=COL>{{cite web |url= https://www.catalogueoflife.org/data/taxon/3G4PZ |title= Gladiolus illyricus W.D.J.Koch |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=n.d. |website=Catalogue of Life |publisher=Species 2000 |access-date=April 17, 2025}}</ref> It is tall [[gladiolus]] that grows up to {{convert|50|cm|sp=us}} tall found in western and southern Europe, particularly around the [[Mediterranean Basin|Mediterranean region]].

In Britain a small population is known in the [[New Forest]] region; Williamson suggests this population may be introduced.<ref name="Ph.D.2014">{{cite book|author=David Pimentel, Ph.D.|title=Biological Invasions: Economic and Environmental Costs of Alien Plant, Animal, and Microbe Species|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=90jRBQAAQBAJ&pg=PA93|date=31 October 2014|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=978-1-4200-4166-8|page=93}}</ref><ref name="Maclean2015">{{cite book|author=Norman Maclean|title=A Less Green and Pleasant Land: Our Threatened Wildlife|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=vmoaCAAAQBAJ&pg=PA129|date=16 April 2015|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-1-316-06227-2|page=129}}</ref> It became a protected species in the UK in 1975 under the Conservation of Wild Creatures and Wild Plants Act.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.caithness.org/caithnessfieldclub/bulletins/1975/october/conservation.htm|title = Caithness CWS - Caithness Field Club - Annual Bulletins - 1975 - October - Conservation}}</ref>
